Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

witty adjective

also funny, humorous, amusing, droll, clever with words

classical

Plaut. Mil. 642: vel cavillātor facētus vel convīva commodus
Cic. Off. 1.108: dulcem et facētum fēstīvīque sermōnis … Sōcratem accēpimus (Lewis & Short)

facētus, facēta, facētum

declension

witty, humorous; fine, elegant

Its noun is facētiae, wit; its adverb facētē.

Other words

  • salsus, salsa, salsum — witty, with a sharp tang (literally salted)

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.228: esse quamvīs facētum atque salsum (Lewis & Short); Quint. 6.3.18: salsum in cōnsuētūdine prō rīdiculō tantum accēpimus (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • vel cavillātor facētus vel convīva commodus item erō

    I can be a witty banterer just as well as an agreeable guestPlaut. Mil. 642–643

See also humour, joke, sarcastic, clever, salty.

SourcesLewis & Short: facetus · Lewis & Short: salio

Plautus, Miles gloriosus 642–643.
